title: Russian APT Poses as Employee of Hacked Firm to Breach Another US Organization
content_md: Russia-linked APT Star Blizzard hacked a US organization by impersonating an employee at another US organization it had previously compromised, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reports. Also tracked as Callisto, Cold Relic, Cold River, UNC4057, and Gossamer Bear, and active for over a decade, Star Blizzard has been formally associated by the US with Russia’s intelligence service FSB. The APT is known for mounting sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns to collect information relevant to the Russian government, and to use victims’ data in attacks on subsequent targets. Star Blizzard “has been highly successful at compromising high-value targets (including government officials, defense contractors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Europe and North America) while maintaining a consistent operational tempo,” Google says. In a recent attack against a US organization, Star Blizzard impersonated an employee of another organization it had breached months earlier. Google, which tracks the group as Cold Relic , believes the hackers likely used contact and relationship information obtained during the earlier intrusion to select and deceive their new target. The first organization was hit in late 2025, using the compromised credentials of a super admin account. The APT leveraged a residential proxy network close to the victim and relied on multi-factor authentication (MFA) push notification fatigue to register a device to the victim’s tenant. Advertisement.
